messages:
John C. (customer): Hey, we're seeing intermittent high latency and some 403s from our integration. We explicitly set region=us-east in the client config but requests keep going to eu-west edge (confirmed by traceroute and response headers). Any idea?
Alisa (support): Sorry you're hitting that — can you paste a minimal repro (curl or SDK) and the response headers you saw?
John C. (customer): Here's a simplified curl we ran from our CI:
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: " \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
Notice the header value is an empty string — that's from our proxy code (we thought blank header would be ignored). Response headers from the call: 
```
x-redwood-edge: eu-west-1
x-request-id: req_9248ab
status: 200 (delayed)
```
Alisa (support): ahhh. Do you also pass region via query param or SDK option? Which SDK/version?
John C. (customer): Using our in-house wrapper around the JS SDK. We pass ?region=us-east in the URL and set options.region = "us-east" in code, but our proxy library sometimes injects an X-Redwood-Region header with empty string when region is not present locally.
Maria (SDK): Thanks for the repro. Historically precedence is: explicit header > SDK option > query param > default routing. We have a bug where an empty X-Redwood-Region header gets treated as a sentinel and triggers fallback logic instead of being ignored — so the routing service falls back to configured customer-default, which for your account is eu.
Ryan (infra): Confirming — load balancer logs show inbound header X-Redwood-Region: ""; our routing service normalizes header values but only checks for header presence, not emptiness in older code paths, so empty string ends up matching the fallback branch. Logged trace: trace=tr_0a3b, routed_to=eu-edge-1.
John C. (customer): That explains it. Workaround for us? Can't immediately change the proxy lib in CI for a few days.
Maria (SDK): Short-term workaround: explicitly set header to the region value (eg `-H "X-Redwood-Region: us-east"`) or remove the header entirely. Also upgrade SDK when we ship the fix — PR is ready.
Alisa (support): I'll escalate — tagging infra to confirm if we can treat empty header as ignored at the ingress layer as a temporary mitigation. @Ryan any perf/regression risk?
Ryan (infra): We can add a quick normalization step that treats empty or whitespace-only X-Redwood-Region as missing. Low risk, but requires a deploy to edge proxies and LB rules. ETA ~4-6 hours if approved.
Maria (SDK): Additional note: the JS SDK change is to coerce empty region values to undefined before sending headers. PR #2896 targets v2.4.3. If you need a pinned workaround earlier, I can publish a patched client build with the coercion as a stopgap (can share a tarball).
John C. (customer): If you can patch at the edge, that works for us. Otherwise we'll set header explicitly in CI. Appreciate the fast turnaround.
Alisa (support): Action items: 1) Ryan to deploy empty-header normalization to edge (opt-in rollback ready) 2) Maria to publish SDK patch & note in release 2.4.3 3) John to apply header change if needed. I'll follow up when infra deploys.
Ryan (infra): Starting a canary deploy to two edges now (eu and us). Will post status.
DeployBot: Deploy started: canary-edge-normalize-empty-region v2026-03-17-001 (canary: eu-west-1, us-east-1)
Ryan (infra): Canary looks good — no increased error rate, routing now ignores empty X-Redwood-Region header and picks SDK option/param. Rolling to remaining edges in 20m.
Alisa (support): John can you confirm after 10-20 minutes that requests from your CI are routing to us-east?
John C. (customer): Confirmed — after ~12m our CI calls hit us-east edge and latency normalized. 403s gone. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Maria (SDK): I'll merge PR and cut v2.4.3, include note in release notes about empty header handling.
Alisa (support): Closing after release and infra roll complete. Leaving thread open for follow-ups.
